we present a CMOS multi-sinewave signal generator that can generate a multi-frequency signal and the required demodulation signals for a synchronous demoderation front-end.

the design of an integrated circuit for a multi-sine generator and demodulator.
the generation and demodulation of multi-sine signals in a CMOS system.
the development of a multi-sine generator for multi-frequency measurements.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed system generates a multi-sine waveform and its corresponding demodulation signals, with a single power supply, using a single chip, without the need for an external summing amplifier, and without the need of any external clocking signals.

the presented system is capable of generating a multi-sine waveform of any desired frequency, amplitude and duration, and at the same time it can provide the 90° and 0° demodulation waveforms required for the synchronous demodulation.

we have designed and implemented a system that is able to generate and demodulate multi-frequency signals, with the ability to generate signals at any desired frequency and with any desired amplitude, with the ability of demodulating each frequency independently, and all in a compact CMOS chip.

the proposed system can be implemented in a standard CMOS process, without the need of additional components.
the proposed system can generate multi-sine signals of any number of components, while the frequency and amplitude can be independently adjusted for each frequency component.
it provides an efficient and cost effective solution for the generation and demodulation of multi-sine signals.
